subject: Request: temporary throughput allowance for AtlasOps holiday launch
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Cc: Maria Gonzales <maria@atlasops.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 08:15:00 -0800
Subject: Request: temporary throughput allowance for AtlasOps holiday launch

Team —

Quick ask: AtlasOps (external contact Maria CC'd) is planning a regionally concentrated launch on Dec 7–10 and is projecting a short 48–72 hour spike that exceeds their current committed capacity. They are requesting a temporary throughput allowance (not a permanent quota change) to cover the peak window.

Summary:
- Expected peak window: 2026-12-07T14:00Z to 2026-12-09T02:00Z (customer local)
- Peak RPS estimate: 120 requests/sec (avg prompt ~350 tokens; completions ~120 tokens)
- Sustained ramp: 3-hour ramp up / 3-hour ramp down each day
- Business impact: payment card onboarding flow for ~120k new users over the window (high priority)

Attached: atlasops_week1_forecast.csv (breaks down hourly projections + sample payload sizes).

Ask: 
1) Can infra/product provision a temporary throughput allowance and a routing policy to pin AtlasOps traffic to Dedicated-2 for the window?
2) If so, what configuration would you need (model variant, max seq, kv cache sizing) and lead time?
3) Ops: can we schedule a dry-run traffic test before Dec 5 (small spike test)?

Maria — we want to make sure we set realistic guardrails so we don't degrade other customers. Team, please reply with feasibility and minimal configuration to support.

Thanks,
Olga
Olga Petrov
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
olga@redwood.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Request: temporary throughput allowance for AtlasOps holiday launch

Thanks Olga — quick clarifying questions before we scope: 

- Which model(s) will AtlasOps be using in production for this flow? (open-llama-7b / redwood-13b-quant / custom)
- Is the 350-token prompt an average, or do you expect long-tail prompts >1k tokens for some flows?
- Do they require streaming responses or is full-response completion acceptable?

If they are on redwood-13b-quant and tokens are mostly <500, provisioning a short-lived Dedicated slot + routing rule looks feasible. If they need streaming and long context, the KV cache and memory ops change the sizing.

Also: Aditya — any constraints from capacity entitlement / commercial side? We should confirm whether this is covered under their current commitment or requires a one-time surge invoice / credit.

-Karthik
Principal Product Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>

Cc: Maria Gonzales <maria@atlasops.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 09:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: temporary throughput allowance for AtlasOps holiday launch

Short answer: technically feasible with caveats.

Notes from infra review:
- If they run redwood-13b-quant with avg 470 total tokens/request (prompt + completion) we estimate ~9–12 tokens/ms CPU on our current VM mix; 120 RPS sustained pushes a dedicated pool of ~6xA100-equivalent capacity for the peak window.
- We can implement a temporary routing rule (policy) that pins their API key to a reserved pool and sets a hard concurrency cap to protect capacity. That rule takes ~24 hours to propagate and must be configured before Dec 5 for a dry-run.
- KV cache: recommend enabling prefix caching for onboarding flows; requires a model-compatible caching key (we'll need sample payloads).

Attachment: burst_config.json (stub) — contains a recommended pool size, concurrency limits, and fallback policy to redwood-7b-ec when capacity is reached.

Open items for the customer: model variant + a sample of high-latency prompts (>1k tokens) so we can validate memory footprint.

I can provision the routing rule and reserve the pool if Product/Commercial sign off the one-off entitlement. Marcus
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

--- Attachment: burst_config.json (JSON, 4KB) ---

Approving from capacity operations side with the following conditions: 

1) Temporary entitlement duration: 2026-12-07T12:00Z through 2026-12-09T04:00Z. No auto-extension.
2) Billing: Commercial to confirm surge pricing or credit (Aditya). If unpaid, we reserve right to throttle at the policy boundary.
3) Dry-run: schedule Tuesday Dec 5 16:00Z (recommended) — Marcus to run a 30-minute 50% scale test.
4) Fallback: if backend latency > 2.5s p95 during dry-run, we revert to redwood-7b-ec for the customer until issues are addressed.

Aditya — please confirm commercial terms and whether we should require a signed surge addendum (I can generate DocuSign if needed).

Laura Bennett
Head of Capacity, Redwood Inference
